full_text_en:
Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Procuratorate v. Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin — dangerous driving case

[Ruling Summary]

According to the provisions of Article 133 (A) of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, where a perpetrator drives a motor vehicle on a road in a racing manner, under vile circumstances, the perpetrator shall be convicted and punished for the crime of dangerous driving.

Procuratorial Authority: Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Zhang Jiwei (nickname "Little Sun"), male, 23 years old, Han ethnicity, college degree, pharmaceutical representative of a certain company, residing at Jiangpu Road, Yangpu District, Shanghai. He was released on bail pending trial on February 6, 2012 in connection with this case.

Defendant: Jin Xin (nickname "Camel"), male, 29 years old, Han ethnicity, university degree, freelancer, residing at Chuansha New Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai. He was released on bail pending trial on February 7, 2012 in connection with this case.

The Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Procuratorate filed a public prosecution with the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court against the defendants Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin, charging them with the crime of dangerous driving.

The indictment alleged: At approximately 20:20 on February 3, 2012, the defendants Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin agreed to meet at Mingxin Racing Service Department, located at No. 99 Leyuan Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai. Thereafter, Zhang Jiwei drove an unlicensed HONGDA (Honda) 1000CC high-power two-wheeled motorcycle, and Jin Xin drove a YAMAHA (Yamaha) high-power two-wheeled motorcycle bearing a fraudulent license plate, Guangdong NL8406. Departing from the said vehicle dealership, they drove to the intersection of Yanggao Road and Jufeng Road, made a U-turn, then traveled south along Yanggao Road, crossed Nanpu Bridge, and proceeded to Lujiabang Road to pick up someone. During the journey, Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin, seeking the thrill of driving high-power two-wheeled motorcycles, exceeded the speed limit on multiple sections of road, ran red lights at several intersections, weaved in and out of lanes to overtake other vehicles, thereby demonstrating their driving skills to each other. When they arrived at the intersection of Lujiabang Road and Henan South Road, they encountered on-duty police officers conducting a check. They then fled by driving along Henan South Road, through Fuxing East Road Tunnel, and along Zhangyang Road, returning to Zhang Jiwei's residence at around 21:00 that evening. After receiving reports from members of the public, the police identified Zhang Jiwei as a major suspect by retrieving street surveillance videos. At approximately 21:00 on February 5, 2012, police arrested Zhang Jiwei at Room 5B, Building 33, Lane 1555, Qishan Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai. Zhang Jiwei truthfully confessed to the facts of his joint racing with Jin Xin and provided the police with Jin Xin's mobile phone number. At approximately 21:00 on February 6, 2012, Jin Xin surrendered to the police after receiving a telephone call from the public security authorities and truthfully confessed the above criminal facts. The procuratorial authority submitted that the acts of Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin in driving motor vehicles on the road in a racing manner, under vile circumstances, had violated Article 133 (A) of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, and that they should be investigated for criminal liability for the crime of dangerous driving, and requested the court to adjudicate the case according to law.

The defendants Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin raised no objections to the above charges during the court trial.

Findings of Fact at First Instance by the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court:

At approximately 20:20 on February 3, 2012, the defendants Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin agreed to ride their motorcycles to "pick up someone and have a ride" and to "enjoy the thrill of these world-class high-power motorcycles." They agreed that "the intersection of Lujiabang Road and Henan South Road was the destination, and whoever arrived first would wait for the other." Subsequently, Zhang Jiwei drove an unlicensed HONGDA (Honda) 1000CC high-power two-wheeled motorcycle (modified), and Jin Xin drove a YAMAHA (Yamaha) high-power two-wheeled motorcycle (modified) bearing a fraudulent license plate, Guangdong NL8406. They departed from the vehicle dealership at No. 99 Leyuan Road, Pudong New Area, traveled to the intersection of Yanggao Road and Jufeng Road, made a U-turn, then traveled south along Yanggao Road, crossed Nanpu Bridge, descended at Lujiabang Road, then proceeded along Henan South Road through Fuxing East Road Tunnel and along Zhangyang Road back to Zhang Jiwei's residence. The total distance was 28.5 kilometers, passing through multiple bus stops, residential communities, schools, and large supermarkets. During the journey, the two defendants repeatedly changed lanes, weaved in and out of dense traffic, ran multiple red lights, and drove at significantly excessive speeds. When they arrived at the intersection of Lujiabang Road and Henan South Road, Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin encountered on-duty police officers conducting a check and fled by driving along Henan South Road, through Fuxing East Road Tunnel, and along Zhangyang Road. Specifically, on the Yanggao South Road – Pujian Road overpass (speed limit 60 km/h), Zhang Jiwei drove at 115 km/h, and Jin Xin drove at 98 km/h; on the Nanpu Bridge deck (speed limit 60 km/h), Zhang Jiwei drove at 108 km/h, and Jin Xin drove at 108 km/h; on the Nanpu Bridge Lujiabang Road approach ramp (speed limit 40 km/h), Zhang Jiwei drove at a speed exceeding 59 km/h, and Jin Xin drove at a speed exceeding 68 km/h; in the Fuxing East Road Tunnel (speed limit 60 km/h), Zhang Jiwei drove at 102 km/h, and Jin Xin drove at 99 km/h.

At approximately 21:00 on February 5, 2012, after defendant Zhang Jiwei was arrested, he truthfully confessed the above facts and provided the public security authorities with defendant Jin Xin's mobile phone number. Jin Xin voluntarily surrendered at approximately 21:00 on February 6, 2012, after receiving a telephone notice from the public security authorities, and truthfully confessed the above facts.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence presented and examined during the trial: testimony of witness Yuan Yijia; testimony and identification record of witness Wang Mingzhou; driving licenses, vehicle licenses, and driver information inquiry results involved in the case; street surveillance videos, screenshots, and explanations from the public security authorities; appraisal opinions from the Shanghai Road Traffic Accident Appraisal Center; work records, arrest records; uniform vehicle sales invoices and vehicle photographs; vehicle information for ordinary motorcycle Guangdong NL8406; detailed historical product information for the vehicle; reply letter from the traffic police brigade of Lufeng City Public Security Bureau; confessions of the two defendants and their household registration information; and other evidence, which are sufficient to establish the facts.

The focus of the dispute in this case is: How to understand and determine the element of "driving a motor vehicle on a road in a racing manner, under vile circumstances" as stipulated in Article 133 (A) of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court):

According to Article 133 (A) of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, where a perpetrator drives a motor vehicle on a road in a racing manner, under vile circumstances, the perpetrator shall constitute the crime of dangerous driving according to law. For a conviction of dangerous driving based on driving a motor vehicle on a road in a racing manner, in addition to the condition of "driving a motor vehicle on a road," the conduct must also satisfy the statutory elements of "racing" and "vile circumstances."

Whether the defendants' conduct constitutes racing. "Racing" as provided by law generally refers to driving behavior where two or more persons, for the purpose of competition, seeking thrills, or other objectives, drive motor vehicles competitively on public roads, urban roads, or other roads, seriously affecting public order and road traffic safety.

In the specific circumstances of this case: First, from the subjective driving mindset: after being brought to justice, the two defendants first confessed to "going out together to hang around, cruise, and have a ride," and later each specifically confessed, "I had an itch, I wanted some enjoyment and excitement," "I hadn't ridden for a while, I had an itch, I wanted to feel the thrill of driving this kind of vehicle, so we went for a ride," "Driving this kind of world-class motorcycle feels comfortable, exciting, and fast," "Enjoying the thrill of this kind of high-power world-class motorcycle." At the same time, the two defendants each confessed, "I just focused on demonstrating my driving skills," "Weaving in and out, overtaking cars on the road gave me psychological satisfaction," when facing red lights, "I believed I could run the red light safely using my vehicle control skills," "I believe in my driving skills," "I don't like using the brakes, I overtake any car in front," "I squeezed through the gap between two cars ahead," "If there was a car in front, I changed lanes and weaved to overtake." The above confessions were corroborated by street surveillance footage, reflecting the competitive psychology of the two defendants in seeking thrills and demonstrating driving skills in this case.

Second, from the route taken: both defendants confessed that the route was mutually agreed upon, starting from No. 99 Leyuan Road, Pudong New Area, to the intersection of Lujiabang Road and Henan South Road to pick someone up, and "whoever arrives first waits for the other." This was also corroborated by the testimony of witness Yuan Yijia and street surveillance footage, demonstrating that the two defendants had jointly agreed upon the starting and ending points of their competitive driving.

Third, from the objective conduct: the defendants' starting point was a racing service department; they drove over-standard high-power modified motorcycles; they engaged in multiple instances of random lane changes, weaving, running red lights, and substantial speeding and other serious traffic violations in pursuit of speed. These objective acts further corroborated the defendants' subjective purpose of driving motor vehicles on the road for competition and thrill-seeking. These objective acts were confirmed by surveillance videos, screenshots, appraisal conclusions, witness testimony, and other evidence on record, and were consistent with the defendants' multiple confessions. Therefore, taken together, the conduct of the two defendants can be found to constitute "racing."

Whether the defendants' conduct constitutes "vile circumstances." "Vile circumstances" as provided by law generally requires a comprehensive assessment based on factors including whether the perpetrator has a driving license, whether the vehicle is a modified high-power vehicle and whether it has a legal license plate, whether there is substantial speeding, whether the racing occurs in congested sections, whether multiple persons race multiple times, whether an accident or panic is caused, whether the perpetrator resists or evades law enforcement, and whether the perpetrator consumes alcohol or drugs leading to impaired control. The core consideration is whether the racing conduct placed public traffic safety in a dangerous state. In this case, although the two defendants held driving licenses, whether their conduct constituted vile circumstances should be determined by a comprehensive assessment of their driving behavior and the degree of violation. First, regarding the vehicles driven: the two defendants drove unlicensed and fraudulently licensed high-power modified motorcycles. Second, regarding the speed: their overall driving speed was very high, exceeding the speed limit by over 50% on multiple sections. Third, regarding the manner of driving: the two defendants repeatedly changed lanes, weaved in front of other vehicles, and ran multiple red lights. Fourth, regarding their attitude toward law enforcement: they fled when police conducted a check. Fifth, regarding the road sections traveled: the routes passed through Yanggao Road, Zhangyang Road, Nanpu Bridge, Fuxing East Road Tunnel, which are all urban arterial roads, viaducts, and tunnels, and also passed by multiple schools, bus and metro stations, residential communities, large supermarkets, and other areas with dense traffic and pedestrian flow. Under the thrill-seeking mindset of high-speed driving and the tense mindset of evading law enforcement, it was highly likely to cause serious and major traffic accidents. The above conduct posed a considerable threat to the life, health, and property safety of an unspecified number of people and effectively placed the public safety of road traffic in a dangerous state. Therefore, it can be found that the conduct of the two defendants in driving motor vehicles on the road in a racing manner constitutes "vile circumstances."

In conclusion, the defendants Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin drove motor vehicles on the road in a racing manner, under vile circumstances, and their conduct constituted the crime of dangerous driving. The charges brought by the procuratorial authority were established. In view of the fact that Zhang Jiwei truthfully confessed the crimes he committed after being brought to justice, he may be given a lighter punishment according to law. In view of the fact that Jin Xin voluntarily surrendered, he also received a lighter punishment according to law. The two defendants committed a joint crime and were both principal offenders; no distinction between principal and accessory was made. During the trial, both defendants recognized the illegality and social harmfulness of their conduct, promised not to engage in dangerous driving again, and repeatedly expressed remorse and repentance. Given that their conduct did not cause actual harmful consequences, and considering all the above circumstances comprehensively, the court applied a suspended sentence according to law.

Accordingly, the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court, in accordance with Article 133 (A), Paragraph 1 of Article 25, Article 53, Article 67, Article 72, and Article 73 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on January 14, 2013:

1. Defendant Zhang Jiwei is convicted of the crime of dangerous driving and sentenced to four months of criminal detention, suspended for four months, and fined RMB 4,000.
2. Defendant Jin Xin is convicted of the crime of dangerous driving and sentenced to three months of criminal detention, suspended for three months, and fined RMB 3,000.

After the judgment was pronounced at first instance, the defendants Zhang Jiwei and Jin Xin did not appeal within the statutory period, and the procuratorial authority did not lodge a protest. The judgment has become legally effective.
